transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

Hello, doctor. I’m so preoccupied with how awful my face and neck look now that I’m starting to avoid the very community things that used to keep me going. My primary care doctor suggested I come speak with you about it.
Can you tell me more about what specifically bothers you about your face and neck, and how long have you been feeling this way?

I'm deeply bothered by the sagging skin and deep lines on my face and neck, which make me feel almost disfigured, especially under bright lights or in photos. These worries actually started back in midlife, but they became much more intense about five years ago after my husband passed away and I began spending more time in well-lit social settings.

Do you experience significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of life due to your concerns about your appearance, or are you more troubled by persistent feelings of fatigue, weakness, or a general inability to recover your energy?

It is definitely the anxiety about my appearance holding me back, not any kind of fatigue or lack of energy. I’ve started turning down art workshops, choir performances, and extra training sessions because I can't stand how I look, which is really hurting my social life and the extra income I was counting on for retirement.

Can you tell me if your concerns about your face and neck are ever accompanied by any repetitive behaviors, such as excessive mirror checking, frequent cosmetic procedures, or a strict skincare routine, that you feel compelled to do in response to these concerns?

Yes, before every workshop or choir practice, I end up spending way too long in the bathroom adjusting my scarf and makeup, leaning in and out of the mirror to find an angle where my neck doesn't look so terrible. I'll constantly take my glasses on and off to check, and I even snap selfies on my phone just so I can zoom in and inspect every single wrinkle.

Do you feel an overwhelming urge to perform these rituals, such as mirror checking or adjusting your appearance, in response to your concerns, or are they more driven by a desire to simply look good or feel more confident in social situations?

It definitely feels like an overwhelming, anxious urge rather than just a normal desire to look good. I feel completely compelled to spend all that time in the bathroom adjusting my scarf, staring in the mirror, and zooming in on selfies just to find some angle where my neck and jaw don't look so awful.
Do you experience any other repetitive thoughts or compulsions beyond those related to your appearance, such as excessive cleaning, ordering, or checking behaviors?
No, I don't experience anything like that at all. My worries and habits are really just completely focused on my face and neck.
